gen-audiowide-gf-cal-sans: Audiowide draws every stroke at a single width, with letters stacked like tiles and generous gaps between them. Cal Sans follows in a friendly sans with the same uniform line, but its tall x-height and short ascenders feel more down to earth.
gen-audiowide-gf-carlito: Futuristic tiles with wide gaps, all in one line width. Carlito, a compact sans with round open letters and big lowercase beside small capitals, keeps a long stretch of text moving smoothly without snagging.
gen-audiowide-gf-changa: Changa reads like a plain sans with cast-iron lowercase, sturdy and tall. Audiowide above it is the real standout, its tile-like glyphs and monoweight lines giving the pair a distinctly futuristic edge.
gen-audiowide-gf-courier-prime: Audiowide's most striking habit is its uniform line, with letters set like tiles and spaced with wide gaps. And Courier Prime, a monospace with the steady line of a drafting pen, handles the precise, structured work that the heading leaves alone.
gen-audiowide-gf-days-one: Tiled, ruler-straight letters with a futuristic hum make Audiowide look like it was built from a kit. Days One takes over below, a sans-serif whose tall x-height fills each line and whose rope-ladder spacing carries a paragraph along steadily.
gen-audiowide-gf-epunda-sans: Epunda Sans reads wide and bright, with generous curves inside each letter. Its trimmed sidebearings keep a paragraph moving smoothly, while Audiowide's laser-etched, constant-width lines make the heading feel unmistakably futuristic.
gen-audiowide-gf-farro: Farro reads as a sturdy sans-serif with compressed ascenders and no stroke contrast at all. And Audiowide, with its tile-like letters and uniform line, lends the heading a futuristic, tech-flavored punch.
gen-audiowide-gf-fragment-mono: Fragment Mono lines its letters up like nails on a ruler, tall and precise. Audiowide's tiled, futuristic shapes then sit above that monospace grid, both fonts keeping an unbroken line with no thick-thin contrast.
gen-audiowide-gf-geist-mono: Audiowide builds its futuristic look from tile-like glyphs with one constant line width, set apart by wide gaps and tall lowercase. Geist Mono sits comfortably beneath, structured and code-like.
gen-audiowide-gf-genos: Audiowide's most distinctive trait is its terminals, which end at the same width they began, giving a futuristic, tiled look. Genos does the quieter reading job, a tightly set sans with a high midline that never snags the eye.
